newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TRACTEBEL,AES SLOW WITH HUNGARY PLANT RETROFITS-MVM.
newsitem.headline: TRACTEBEL,AES SLOW WITH HUNGARY PLANT RETROFITS-MVM.

text.p: Utilities Tractebel and AES denied allegations by Hungary's electricity supplier MVM they had failed to honour commitments to submit plans to refurbish Hungarian plants in which they hold stakes.

MVM's strategic director Istvan Bakacs told Reuters the two companies' failure to put forward concrete plans to retrofit their Hungarian units meant MVM could not offer them new power purchase agreements (PPAs).

"Unfortunately for over a year (the two companies) have not honoured their obligations in the privatisation agreement," he said. "They were obliged to go ahead with the preparation of the retrofit programme and negotiate a new supply agreement -- they haven't started anything."
Tractebel bought a 49 percent stake in Dunamenti power station in central Hungary in December 1995 while AES took an 80 percent stake in the Tisza plant, in eastern Hungary, eight months later.
Both have been negotiating with MVM to revise the current PPAs, which they view as insufficient to generate the profits they were promised when they bought into the sector.

German consortium RWE Energie AG and EVS AG, which bought into the Matra plant in northeast Hungary also in 1995, said on Wednesday it had reached its own 18-year PPA with MVM on the basis of a programme announced in June to begin retrofitting three of the Matra's five 200 megawatt(MW) blocks.
"This is a total investment which is worth 450 million marks," Bakacs said. "If the other companies commit themselves to a similar retrofitting they can count on a similar PPA," Bakacs added.
As well as RWE/EVS's coal-fired Matra power station, Tractebel and AES also operate five other 150-200MW blocks due for retrofit at Dunamenti and Tisza.

Bakacs said Matra had originally been bottom of the list for refurbishing as its boilers were in the best physical state but had leapfrogged the other sites because it had been the only company to commit itself to refurbishment.
"Only Matra went ahead and committed to the new investment and they secured licenses already," he said. "We sat down three months ago for this PPA and we managed to sign it in three months."
AES's project development manager Richard Mardon told Reuters he was surprised at Bakacs's remarks.
"There are 10 units throughout Hungary and you can't take them all out at once to be refitted. The Tisza 2 retrofit was never planned to be done until 2002/2003," he said.

"We have not broken any privatisation agreements because the timetable laid down (for retrofits) was much longer than it is now. We are now realising that you can jump the queue and push the project to an earlier time frame," he said.
"There's been a bit of a communication problen with MVM," he said. "We are now beginning to move (on the retrofit) -- we just didn't realise they wanted it quite so soon."

Tractebel's managing director for Hungary Tibor Kuhl also denied his company had broken its privatisation contract, saying he had signed an agreement with MVM earlier this year formally delaying the Dunamenti retrofit until after the Matra refurbishment.
"An agreement was reached in early 1997 on delaying the retrofit since MVM suggested that other power stations might be ready earlier," he told Reuters on Friday.
He added that RWE's PPA may have been easier to reach as Matra has its own lignite fuel supplies while oil-fired Dunamenti has to secure its supplies of oil from Hungarian oil company MOL.

According to the Matra PPA, MVM will initially buy electricity at 7.60 forints per kilowatt/hour, with quarterly adjustments to be made by the Hungarian Energy Office in line with a price formula taking into account world market prices, Hungarian production costs and the forint/dollar exchange rate.
The agreement also clears the way for RWE to prepare the construction of two new lignite-powered 500 MW power plants worth three billion marks at nearby Bukkabrany.
The new plants would be in line with the second of two open tenders MVM announced last week for a total 2,000 MW of new capacity
"This (PPA) problem has been solved," an RWE source told Reuters. "Now we can go ahead with the development project in Bukkabrany."

AES's Mardon declined to disclose his company's precise plans for the new tender but Kuhl said Tractebel would be submitting proposals in the first purely technical stage of the bidding over the next two months.
Bakacs told Reuters earlier formal bidding, including price and costs, would start next year.
